what_its_for: Asciminib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in adults. It works by blocking a protein called BCR-ABL1 that causes cancer cells to grow out of control. It is used when other cancer medicines have not worked well enough or could not be tolerated.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablets. Take asciminib on an empty stomach — do not eat anything for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after taking your dose. Try to take it at the same time(s) every day to keep it in your system at a steady level.
dosing: The most common dose is 40 mg (two 20 mg tablets) taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Some patients take a higher dose of 200 mg twice a day depending on their specific situation. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still more than 12 hours until your next scheduled dose. If your next dose is less than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store asciminib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect them from moisture and heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat food within 2 hours before or 1 hour after taking your dose. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can raise the level of this medicine in your blood and cause more side effects. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with asciminib. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least a few weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you have: chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling (possible heart or blood vessel problems); sudden severe headache, vision changes, or numbness (possible stroke or bleeding); unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat; severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; skin rash or allergic reaction such as hives or trouble breathing; feeling very tired, pale, or short of breath (possible low blood counts); or pain, swelling, or redness in your joints or muscles.
when_it_works: Asciminib begins working in your body right away, but it may take several weeks to months before your doctor sees improvement in your lab results. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check how well the medicine is working. Do not stop taking asciminib without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use asciminib if you are pregnant — it can harm or cause birth defects in an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. It is not known if asciminib passes into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have serious kidney or liver disease. Children: Asciminib is currently approved only for adults. Older adults (65+): This medicine can be used in older adults, but you may need closer monitoring for side effects.
